title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
statement: Merge two sorted linked lists, given as value arrays, into one sorted list. Return the merged values.
hints: A dummy head removes the empty-list special case.
Always attach the smaller current node, and advance that list only.
When one list ends, attach the other list in one pointer assignment.

approaches.name: Pointer merge
approaches.explanation: Rewire existing nodes. The output list is the extra structure the caller asked for.

editorial: This is the merge step of merge sort, played on nodes. Compare the two heads, splice the smaller one onto the tail, and repeat. The unused list is already sorted, so it becomes the final suffix.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def merge_two_lists(list1: list[int], list2: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    a = _node_chain(list1)
    b = _node_chain(list2)
    dummy = _node_chain([0])
    tail = dummy
    while a is not None and b is not None:
        if a.value <= b.value:
            tail.nxt = a
            a = a.nxt
        else:
            tail.nxt = b
            b = b.nxt
        tail = tail.nxt
    tail.nxt = a if a is not None else b
    return _to_list(dummy.nxt)
